title: At the table
subtitle: Serving and pairing Chardonnay
objectives: Pair different Chardonnay styles with food

steps.title: Match the style
steps.body: Lean Chablis suits oysters, shellfish and goat's cheese. Rich, oaked Chardonnay suits lobster, roast chicken, creamy sauces and pork. Tropical, warm-climate Chardonnay suits grilled chicken and mildly spiced dishes. Blanc de Blancs suits sushi, caviar and fried food.
steps.highlight: Chablis with oysters; oaked with lobster

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve lean Chardonnay at 8 to 10 degrees, rich oaked styles at 10 to 13. Most New World Chardonnay is best within three to five years. Grand Cru Chablis and Côte de Beaune age 10 to 20 years, developing honey, nuts and mushroom. Premature oxidation, or premox, affected some Burgundy from the 1990s.

steps.prompt: Which Chardonnay style suits oysters best?
steps.explanation: Chablis' acidity and saline edge match oysters.

steps.body: Serve rich, oaked Chardonnay slightly warmer than other whites. Too cold, its texture and aromas close up.

steps.prompt: Some Burgundy whites from the 1990s suffered from premature oxidation.
steps.explanation: Yes. Premox affected some vintages, with wines browning and losing fruit early.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Match the Chardonnay style to the dish
Serve lean styles colder, rich ones a little warmer
